function: PPO learns NOMA user scheduling and hybrid IRS working mode (reflection coefficient) for secrecy rate; AO with SDR sets IRS phases and AP receive beamformer (p. 5-6).
system: Uplink secure NOMA, AP with 4 antennas, single-antenna users and eavesdropper, hybrid passive/active IRS with energy harvesting, N=10-30 elements; frequency not stated (p. 3, p. 9).
method: Dual-cycling DRL: outer PPO actor-critic DNNs learn scheduling and IRS mode online from state (CSI, IRS energy); inner AO or lightweight two-phase optimization; asynchronous update (p. 5-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: quasi-static Rayleigh flat fading with distance-based path loss, randomly placed users; no standard channel model or public dataset (p. 4, p. 9).
test_conditions: Fig. 4 convergence at N=30, T=30, K=5; secrecy rate swept over IRS elements, channel variance, IRS location, transmit power, user number; no separate train/test split reported (p. 9-12).
baselines: Learned: P-DRL [24] (PPO decides all variables); non-learned: random IRS phases (R-IRS), passive-only IRS, active-only IRS, random mode, pure NOMA, pure OMA (p. 9, p. 11).
metrics: Secrecy rate (average reward) versus episodes, IRS elements, channel variance, IRS location, transmit power, user number; mode-selection ratios; AO/TP run-time ratio (p. 9-12).
complexity: Two-phase O({max{K,N}^4*N^0.5*log(1/e)}^2) versus AO times L1*L2; PPO cost from layer sizes (eq. 26); AO/TP run-time ratio 1.2x-2.4x; 2 min per inner update (p. 6, 8-9).
openness: none (the only link is the CVX solver, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "We consider that all channels follow quasistatic Rayleigh flat-fading"; the channels come from the authors' own simulator with a distance-based path loss (p. 9), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "To simulate various wireless environments, we vary the channel variance"; the paper sweeps system parameters (p. 9-12) but never states that a trained policy is tested on a condition unseen in training, and reports no adaptation.
q3_support: p. 9: "we consider the pure DRL (P-DRL) scheme [24] as the benchmark" (earlier learned design, PPO for all variables) and "the random IRS (R-IRS) with randomly configured phases" (non-learned); both compared on secrecy rate (Figs. 4, 6).
q4_support: p. 8: "We further compare the computational complexity of the AO and the two-phase algorithms", with complexity orders for both and for the PPO networks (eq. 26); p. 9 reports the measured AO/TP run-time ratio of 1.2x to 2.4x.
q5_support: p. 9: "The users are randomly distributed within a rectangular area" shows simulated data only; no link or DOI to code or data, the only URL is the CVX solver (p. 13: "http://cvxr.com/cvx").
notes: Included, area 3: the PPO agent chooses the hybrid IRS working mode (reflection coefficient) jointly with NOMA user scheduling, a physical-layer decision with an above-physical one; IRS phases and AP receive beamformer come from AO with SDR, not from learning, so the reviewer should confirm the function. P-DRL [24] is read as an earlier learned method (PPO for all variables) but could be seen as an ablation of the proposed framework (q3). No train/test split or unseen condition is stated (q2). Complexity formulas and Fig. 5 were read from the page images (p. 8-9).
